summary: Standardize ephemeral workspace creation and autosweeper for feature pods
description:
Issue summary:
We need a standardized, auditable automation that provisions ephemeral Slack channels, Confluence draft spaces/pages, and temporary Jira groups when a feature pod requests a sandbox workspace. The automation should attach an owner, enforce RBAC, and schedule an automatic review/archival (autosweeper) after a configurable TTL (default 30 days).

Background / why: 
Feature teams frequently create ad-hoc channels and Confluence pages for short-lived experiments. Lack of standardization causes orphaned channels, inconsistent permissions, and audit gaps. Security and Platform would like a predictable lifecycle that reduces noise and improves cost/retention hygiene.

Impact: 
- Cross-pod clutter in Slack and Confluence; difficulty finding active workspaces.
- Manual cleanup burden on Platform and SRE.
- Potential permission drift and audit holes (unknown owners).

Request: 
1) Implement a lightweight self-serve flow (Slack slash command + Jira form) that creates: a named ephemeral Slack channel (private by default), a Confluence draft space or page created from a template, and a Jira group with scoped view permissions.
2) On creation, require an explicit owner (email) and set metadata tags: pod, feature, ttl-days.
3) Autosweeper: after TTL expires, automated job posts a 7-day warning in the channel, then archives Slack channel and sets Confluence space/page to read-only and not searchable. Create a small audit artifact (confluence note / jira task) capturing the action.
4) RBAC/Compliance: integrate with existing role-sync; owners must belong to an org group; deny creation if owner is not in an allowed list for private workspaces.
5) Provide a Confluence runbook and a short onboarding doc for product leads.

Scope and constraints: 
- Must reuse existing Slack-bots infra; do not introduce new long-lived credentials.
- The automation must emit an event to our audit topic (kafka/audit-events) for every create/modify/archive action.
- Default TTL = 30 days; allow override per-request up to 90 days (enterprise exceptions handled via manual process).

Acceptance notes: see acceptance_criteria field.

Operational handover expectations:
- Include a runbook with playbook steps to reverse archive, reassign owner, and override TTL for enterprise requests.
- Provide a migration/cleanup plan for 60-day backlog of orphaned pods (separate follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Provisioning flow: ability to create workspace via Slack slash command and Jira form with owner, pod, and ttl metadata recorded.
RBAC enforcement: creation blocked if owner is not in allowed identity group for private workspaces.
Audit events: every create/modify/archive emits a record to kafka/audit-events with workspace id and actor.
Autosweeper behavior: 7-day warning -> archive Slack channel + set Confluence to read-only -> create audit note. Verified in a staging test with ttl=2 days.
Runbook and docs: public runbook created and reviewed by Security and Internal Tools; 1 pager for product leads published in Confluence.
Graceful override: Platform staff can extend TTL via admin Jira action; extension events are audited.
